summary: Washington County, VT wooden tower built 1933-34 by CCC men; lightning destroyed it in 1944; steel tower dismantled late 1970s; cabin and anchor plates reported in 1996, cabin in 2012.

facts.design: Wooden tower with cabin (1933-44); steel four-legged tower with glass-enclosed cab from 1947 until dismantled
facts.status_note: Steel tower dismantled in the late 1970s. The 1996 history says anchor plates and bolts remain in the ledge; the summit cabin stood in 1996 and 2012.

access.note: Summit is on privately owned land. Landowners closed the old trail and the 2012 blog describes signs against parking at the trailhead. No public access arrangement found.

facts.agency: Vermont State Forest Service (state forestry department)

events.note: Completed by CCC men for the State Forest Service in autumn 1933 (Sept and Oct 1933 newspapers). The 1996 history dates the wooden tower and cabin to 1934 from Forest Service records.
Lightning storm struck the wooden tower in August 1944; local men put out the fire on the mountain.
Wooden tower destroyed by lightning (Barre Daily Times and Burlington Free Press, August 1944). The 1996 history gives 1947.
Northfield woman employed by the state as fire warden at the Mount Alice tower, July 1944.
Steel fire tower erection supervised in September 1947 to replace the burned tower.
1949-50 Vermont Forest Service biennial report: old wooden tower removed. Year given is the first year of the report period.
Frederick Fuller stationed at the lookout for the Department of Forestry (Burlington Free Press, May 1961).
Boy Scouts bought the cabin from the state forestry department for one dollar.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Newspapers from September and October 1933 say the tower was completed or built that autumn; the 1996 local history says Forest Service records show 1934. The story gives the 1933 newspaper date and notes the 1934 claim.

Newspapers from August 1944 report the wooden tower destroyed by lightning, and a September 1947 item refers to the fire 'a few years ago'. The 1996 local history says 1947 from memory. The story follows the 1944 newspapers and notes the conflict.

notes_for_editor: Dates disagree. The 1933 build and 1944 lightning come from newspapers transcribed on the Forest Lookouts page; the 1996 local history gives 1934 and 1947. The story follows the newspapers and says so. The 1996 year comes from the file name, and the text includes the words 'In 1996 we can undertake a journey'. The transcription spells the 1944 warden 'Louis'; the story leaves the name out. The steel tower's removal is dated only to 'the late 70s', so no event year is given for it. The 15.2 m height is the 1969 steel tower; the 1933 wooden tower was 35 feet per the newspaper. Access is set to permission from the landowner statements; no permit rule is stated. An AllTrails search snippet mentions concrete footings at the summit, but the page returned HTTP 403, so it is not used. Used 2 WebSearch calls and about 6 page reads.
